A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-modality and HC-M3D study. Their complete main text, appendices, tables, and figures support reliable comparison; back-matter reflow does not obscure substantive content.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-perturbation experiments, HC-M3D evaluations, visual-encoder comparisons, and hallucination analyses, including supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The visual-perturbation procedures, HC-M3D construction, encoder-combination strategies, and MathPOPE design are unchanged. The appendix image-token interleaving procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training corpora, mathematical and general VQA benchmarks, 1,851-sample HC-M3D dataset, and MathPOPE coverage. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including G-LLaVA, MathLLaVA, MAVIS, MultiMath, general language/vision-language models, and visual-encoder variants.

E3.justification: The evaluation splits, model configurations, three-stage training schedules, perturbation controls, sample sizes, and metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3–6 and Appendix C/Table 11.

E4.justification: Both retain image and option perturbation studies, encoder-combination and interleaving analyses, POPE/MathPOPE hallucination evaluations, and visual case examples. Appendix A moves across a page boundary without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix C reports random seed 42 in both versions. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, with no added repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout Tables 1–13 and the figures. For example, Table 5 retains ALL accuracies of 49.2 for MultiMath and 49.0 for GPT-4o; Appendix Table 10 retains averages of 36.9, 34.0, and 35.0 for its three encoder configurations.

T1.justification: Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. Existing metric definitions and mathematical reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about weak visual reliance, textual shortcuts, HC-M3D's contribution, and the difficulty of improving mathematical reasoning through encoder combinations.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications, and limitations are retained. Section 3.2 replaces 'image generation tasks' with 'VQA tasks' within an already-established VQA comparison; this corrects terminology without introducing a new interpretation.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgment states that computations used Fudan University's CFFF platform, adding computing provenance. It does not establish a change to the hardware or training procedure; Appendix C/Table 11 and the benchmark/code access statement otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. Differences in reference placement result from reflow after the acknowledgment is inserted.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the isolated 'image generation' wording to 'VQA,' adds an acknowledgment with reviewer thanks and corresponding-author information, and changes byline markers. The research narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment causes localized back-matter reflow: Appendix A starts on page 13 instead of page 12, and Tables 9–10 shift within page 13. Figures, table structures, captions, and displayed scientific content are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Section 3.2's task label to VQA improves precision, and naming the CFFF platform adds limited computing provenance. These provide modest clarity and documentation gains; the empirical evidence, methods, and limitations remain unchanged.
